items.item: 3rd Quarter Fire Department Operations Update
items.why: The Fire Department is presenting its quarterly report on operations and activities.

items.item: Police Department General Operations Update
items.why: The Police Department is presenting general updates on department operations.

items.item: Police Officer and Fire Lieutenant Hiring
items.why: The Commission will interview five candidates for Police Officer and one candidate for promotion to Lieutenant in a closed session where personnel matters are discussed privately.

items.item: Citizen Complaint Reconsideration Request
items.why: The Commission will consider a request to reconsider dismissal of a citizen complaint against a specific person in a closed session.

items.item: Deputy Chief Hiring Process Listening Session
items.why: Police Department employees will participate in a listening session about the hiring process for Deputy Chief in a closed session.

preview.overview: The Police & Fire Commission is scheduled to hear operational updates from both departments and interview candidates for police officer and fire lieutenant positions in a closed session.

items.item: Bikeshare program ridership data and spring promotion plans
items.why: The committee will discuss how the city's bikeshare program is performing and plans for promoting it in spring.

items.item: Community Sustainability Survey results
items.why: The committee will review results from a community survey about sustainability.

items.item: MPO Bike/Ped Subcommittee update and bike counter data
items.why: The committee will receive updates from the regional MPO (metropolitan planning organization) subcommittee on biking and walking, plus bike counter data.

items.item: Pavement conditions on Adolph Street and River Edge Parkway
items.why: The committee will discuss road surface conditions on these two routes used by bikers and pedestrians.

items.item: Police Department attendance and enabling language
items.why: The committee will receive an update on Police Department participation and language enabling their involvement.

items.item: Rectangular rapid flashing beacon on Thomas Street and River Edge Parkway
items.why: The committee will discuss a RRFB (a flashing pedestrian crossing signal) planned for this intersection.

preview.overview: The Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee will review the city's bikeshare program performance and discuss conditions on key biking and walking routes around town.

items.item: Seven 2027 budgets for housing programs and facilities
items.why: The board is asked to vote on separate budgets for the Housing Choice Voucher Program, Public Housing Program, Riverview Terrace, Riverview Towers LLC, Fulton Street, and 8th Avenue.

items.item: Repositioning public housing scattered sites to voucher program
items.why: The board is asked to vote on Resolution #26-012 to convert scattered public housing sites to project-based vouchers after a consultant presents repositioning options.

items.item: Riverview Towers façade repair bids
items.why: The board is asked to discuss and vote on bids received for masonry and concrete façade repairs at Riverview Towers LLC.

items.item: Sub-recipient agreement for 405 S 8th Avenue property
items.why: The board is asked to discuss and vote on a rental property agreement between the city and the authority for 405 S 8th Avenue.

items.item: Capital needs assessment for scattered sites properties
items.why: The board is asked to discuss and vote on a request for proposals for a capital needs assessment of scattered public housing sites.

items.item: Presentation on repositioning options for scattered sites
items.why: S.C. Koegler Consulting will present comprehensive repositioning options for the authority's scattered public housing sites.

preview.overview: The Community Development Authority is scheduled to vote on seven budgets for housing programs and facilities. The board will also consider reshaping its public housing scattered sites program and approve repair bids for Riverview Towers.

items.item: Animal impoundment services agreement with Humane Society
items.why: The committee will vote to approve a contract with the Humane Society of Marathon County for the city to use their animal impoundment services.

items.item: Five other service and equipment purchase agreements
items.why: The committee will vote to approve agreements for mapping software (Esri), county production services, cemetery operations, and fire department cardiac monitors and ventilators.

items.item: Budget change and lift purchase for Athletic Park
items.why: The committee will vote to approve a budget modification and sole source request to buy an outdoor vertical platform lift for Athletic Park.

items.item: Update on county pet license fee changes for 2027
items.why: City staff will update the committee on how Marathon County plans to change pet license fees starting in 2027.

preview.overview: The Finance Committee is scheduled to vote on six agreements and contracts for city services. These include animal impounding, mapping software, cemetery operations, and fire department equipment purchases.

items.item: 2026 budget modification for year-end projections
items.why: The Finance Committee is asking the council to approve various budget adjustments based on how the year ended.

items.item: Salary structure revision for general city employees
items.why: The Finance Committee and Human Resources Committee are asking the council to revise how general employees' salaries are structured.

items.item: Special assessments for 2027 street construction projects
items.why: The Infrastructure & Facilities Committee is asking the council to levy special assessments (charges to property owners) to pay for street work in 2027.

items.item: Deed restrictions and non-conforming uses at 1300 Cleveland Avenue
items.why: The Economic Development Committee is asking the council to approve deed restrictions and clarify existing non-conforming uses on city-owned property.

items.item: Driveway and concrete approach exceptions for Kolbe & Kolbe Millwork
items.why: The Infrastructure & Facilities Committee is asking the council to approve oversized driveways and waive a concrete approach requirement at three nearby addresses on South 11th Avenue.

items.item: District 9 aldermanic vacancy
items.why: The Common Council is addressing how to fill an empty aldermanic seat in District 9.

preview.overview: The Common Council will vote on the 2026 budget modification and several resolutions affecting city property and employee pay. The council will also meet in closed session to discuss litigation strategy.

items.item: Recommendation for 2026 demolition of 207 North 1st Avenue
items.why: The board will decide whether to recommend demolition of the building at 207 North 1st Avenue (MBX South). Bids were opened on November 17.

items.item: Pay estimates for lift station and street projects
items.why: The board will approve four contractor payments: a second payment for Crocker Street Lift Station work, final payment for Cherry Street Lift Station, first payment for downtown sidewalk improvements, and final payment for asphalt paving project.

preview.overview: The Board of Public Works is scheduled to decide whether to recommend demolition of a building at 207 North 1st Avenue. The board will also approve payments for several street and utility projects around the city.

weston.name: Mountain Bay Metropolitan Police Oversight Board

items.item: Aquatic Center Repairs update
items.why: Director Osterbrink will report on ongoing leak detection and equipment replacement work by Neuman Pools, including the status of concrete repairs needed to fix identified leaks in the pool system.

items.item: Farmers Market End of Season Survey results
items.why: The committee will review feedback from 129 survey responses about the market's move to Kennedy Park this season. Results show mixed views on parking, traffic flow, and shade, with strong praise for vendor selection and community atmosphere.

items.item: Kennedy Park Master Plan discussion
items.why: The committee will discuss next steps for the master plan in light of the farmers market's permanent location at the park and ongoing planning by DCE Youth Hockey for the northwest corner.

preview.overview: The Parks and Recreation Committee will hear updates on aquatic center repairs and discuss survey results from this season's farmers market at Kennedy Park. The committee may decide how to respond to parking and traffic concerns raised by both vendors and the public.

items.item: 4K Program Agreements for 2027-2028 school year
items.why: The board is asked to approve formal agreements with Wausau Child Care, Mountain View Montessori, Newman Catholic Schools - St. Michael, and two prior partner sites for the four-year-old kindergarten program.

items.item: Staff turnover and retention report for all employee groups
items.why: Tabatha Gundrum will present data on turnover and retention across the district and discuss plans to address findings in the coming year.

items.item: Review and approve 44 district policies and technical corrections
items.why: The board is asked to review and approve updates to policies covering curriculum, student conduct, health services, transportation, and other district operations.

items.item: 2026-2027 student demographic report
items.why: The Director of Technology will present enrollment and demographic data for the upcoming school year.

items.item: Referendum budget summary updates
items.why: The Assistant Superintendent of Operations will update the board on spending progress related to the recent referendum.

items.item: Adjusted 6-12th grade social studies scope and sequence
items.why: The board is asked to approve changes to the social studies curriculum for grades 6 through 12.

preview.overview: The school board is scheduled to approve new agreements for the district's four-year-old kindergarten program with community partners. The board will also hear updates on staff turnover, student demographics, and budget progress from the recent referendum.
The Wausau School Board is scheduled to hold a special meeting with no items for public discussion. All business will occur in closed session.

items.item: 2027 Budget for City of Mosinee
items.why: The Common Council will hold a public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget, then vote on Resolution No. 2026-08 to adopt it and authorize the tax levy.

items.item: Building Permit Applications
items.why: The Common Council will discuss and decide on building permit applications.

items.item: City Employee Holiday Gift Certificates
items.why: The Common Council will discuss and decide on holiday gift certificates for city employees.

items.item: Police Labor Agreement Modification
items.why: The Common Council will discuss and decide on changes to the labor agreement with the Mosinee Professional Police Association.

preview.overview: Mosinee residents can hear and comment on the city's 2027 budget at a public hearing. The Common Council is scheduled to vote on approving the budget and authorizing the tax levy.
